questions.question: Who among the following medieval rulers focused his attention on the construction of sarai (shelter) for the convenience of travelers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Sher Shah Suri.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sher Shah Suri, a medieval ruler, focused on the construction of sarai for the convenience of travelers.**
 
• **Sarai were shelters that provided food, water, and lodging for travelers, especially those on long journeys.**
 
• Sher Shah Suri built a network of saris along the** **main roads and highways in his empire, which facilitated travel and trade.
 
• The construction of saris was a significant achievement of Sher Shah Suri's reign, as it improved the infrastructure of the empire and benefited the common people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Babur was more interested in military conquests.**

 
 
• The Mughal Empire** **in the Indian subcontinent was founded by Babur.
 
 
 
• **Akbar was interested in religious tolerance and administrative reforms.**
 
 
• The reign of Akbar, the third Mughal emperor, lasted from **1556 to 1605.**
 
 
 
• **Humayun was interested in restoring his lost empire.**
 
 
• From 1530 to 1540 and again from 1555 until his death in 1556, Humayun, the second Mughal emperor, ruled over regions that are today Eastern Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Northern India, and Pakistan.

questions.question: Who among the following was the creator of Raga Darbari Canada and the court poet of Akbar's court during the Mughal period in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Mian Tansen.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tansen**, also mention to as **Miyan Tan Sen or Ramtanu Pande, **was a important body of Hindustani classical music.
 
• Born in a **Hindu brahmin family,** he learnt his art in the northwest region of **modern Madhya Pradesh.**
 
• He was greatly respected for **his dhrupad and raga compositions and for his vocal performances**.
 
• He joined **the court of the Mughal emperor Akbar,** who was famous for his patronage of the arts.
 
• Tansen became **one of the navratnas (“nine gems”), a collection of the most talented intellectuals and artists in the court**. His expertise was honoured with the title Mian (“Master”).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bilaskhani Todi** is a Hindustani classical raga.​ 
 
• **Swami Haridas **was a spiritual poet and classical musician.
 
• **Baiju Bawra **(Lit. "Baiju the Insane", born as Baijnath Mishra) was a **dhrupad musician from medieval India**.

questions.question: The city of Fatehpur Sikri was built by _______.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Akbar**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** royal city at Fatehpur Sikri **was built by the Mughal emperor Akbar__ during the **second half of the 16th century.**
 
• It was celebrated as the city of Victory of the **Mughal Empire, **which was the capital city for more than 10 years from 1571 to 1585.
 
• It was turned as Fatehabad (the city of Victory) where the legendary sons of Akbar were born.
 
• It’s also known for the complex of monuments and temples all in uniform architectural style.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**__Akbar (1542- 1605)__

__
 
• He reigned from 1556 to 1605.
 
• He constructed Fatehpur Sikri and made it his capital in 1569.
 
• Buland Darwaza was constructed at the gate.
 
• He started a new religion Din-i Ilahi in 1581-82.
 
• Abul Fazl wrote his biography titled Akbarnama.
 
• Nine of his courtiers were known as Navratnas.
 
 
• They were Todar Mal, Abul Fazal, Faizi, Birbal, Tansen, Abdur Rahim Khana-i-Khana, Mullah-do-Pyaza, Raja Man Singh, and Fakir Aziao-Din.
 
 
 
• He married a Hindu princess Harka Bai who is commonly known as Jodha Bai.
 
• Akbar captured the historic fortress of Chitor in 1568.
 
• He abolished the pilgrimage tax by Hindus in 1563.
 
• He also abolished the Jizyah tax in 1564.
 
• He also introduced the Mansabdari System or the rank-holder system to organize the nobility and army.

Aurangzeb (1658 AD-1707 AD):

 
• Aurangzeb defeated Dara at Dharmat (1658 AD), Samugarh (1658 AD), and Deorai, in which Samugarh was the decisive one and Deorai was the last one.
 
• After the victory, Aurangzeb was crowned at Delhi under the title *Alamgir*. He died in February 1707 in Ahmadnagar.
 
• Aurangzeb captured Guru Teg Bahadur, the 9th Guru of Sikhs in 1675 AD and executed him when he refused to embrace Islam.
 
 
• The 10th and last Sikh Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, son of Guru Teg Bahadur, organized his followers into a community of warriors called *Khalsa* to fight against the Muslims.
 
 
 
• Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj was the most powerful Maratha king and an arch-enemy of Aurangzeb.
 
• The Mughal conquests reached a climax during Aurangzeb’s reign as Bijapur and Golconda were annexed in 1686 AD and 1687 AD, respectively.
 
• Under him, the Mughal empire reached its greatest extent and the largest single-state ever known in India.
 
• He forbade the inscription of *Kalma *on the coins, also forbade sati and Jharokha-darshan.
 
• He ended the celebration of Navroz and, in 1679 AD, reimposed Jizya. 

Shah Jahan:

 
• On 5 January 1592, Shahab-ud-din Muhammad Khurram, later known as Shah Jahan, was born to Mughal Emperor Jahangir and his wife Jagat Gosaini.
 
• Shah Jahan was an able military commander. 
 
• On becoming the emperor, Shah Jahan executed many of his former rivals including his own brother Shahryar. 
 
• Before becoming king, as a prince, he had been the governor of the Deccan, Bihar, Bengal, Gujarat, and Delhi.
 
• As king, Shah Jahan expanded the military and promoted the production of arms. He annexed several territories.
 
• Shah Jahan married multiple times as was the custom.
 
• His favorite was said to be Arjumand Banu Begum who is better known as Mumtaz Mahal.
 
• She died during childbirth in 1631 and Shah Jahan was said to be depressed.
 
• He got the Taj Mahal built in her honor and perhaps, he is most famous for this architectural feat.
 
• He also created many other architectural marvels including the Pearl Mosque at Agra, the Red Fort, the Jama Masjid at Delhi, the Shalimar Gardens, and some other buildings in present Pakistan.
 
• He also got the famous Peacock Throne built.

Jahangir__

 
• In 1605, Prince Salim succeeded with the title Jahangir (Conqueror of World) when he assumed the throne after the death of Akbar.
 
• He issued 12ordinances. He is known for his strict administration of justice.
 
• He established Zanjir-i-Adil (chain of justice) at Agra for the seekers of royal justice.
 
• He is the eldest son of Akbar was born at Fatehpur Sikri near Agra in 1569.
 
• In 1611, he married Mehr-un-Nisa whom he gave the title of Nur Jahan (light of the world).
 
• Nurjahan exercised tremendous influence over state affairs. She was made the official Badshah Begum. 
 
• Jahangir issued coins jointly in Nurjahan's name and his own.
 
• Jahangir also married Manbai in 1585 AD and Jodhbai in 1587 AD.
 
• He defeated and imprisoned his son, Khusrau Mirza.
 
• He also beheaded Guru Arjun, the 5th Sikh Guru and one of the supporters of Khusrau Mirza.
 
• Captain Hawkins (1608-1611) and Sir Thomas Roe (1615-1616) visited Jahangir's court.
 
• Production of Tobacco started in his reign.
 
• He wrote his autobiography Tuzuk-i-Jahangir.
 
• He was buried in Lahore in 1627.

questions.question: In which language were the Mughal court chronicles written?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Persian.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Mughal court chronicles were written in Persian.
 
• **​**__Mughal chronicles such as the **Akbar Nama** were written in Persian, while others, like Babur's memoirs, were translated from Turkish into the Persian Babur Nama.
 
• **Urdu **came from the amalgamation of **Persian with Hindavi. **
 
• Chronicles commissioned by the Mughal emperors are an important source for studying the empire and its court.
 
• The authors of Mughal chronicles were mostly courtiers.
 
• The Mughals were **Chaghtai Turks** by origin.
 
• **Turkish **was their **mother tongue** hence the first ruler Babur wrote poetry and his memoirs in this language.

questions.question: Who among the following Khayal singers of 19th century was given the title of ‘Tanras” by Bahadur Shah Jaffar, the last Mughal Emperor of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Meer Qutub Baksh__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**__**Meer Qutub Baksh**__

__
 
• **Meer Qutub Baksh** alias **'Tanrus Khan**' was an iconic **Khayal singer of the 19th century.**
 
• He was an** Indian musician** of the Hindustani Classical tradition known for being a luminary of the** Delhi Gharana.**
 
• He was a** court musician** and** music teacher** to **the last Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar II.**
 
• Tanrus Khan was famous for his swift, sparkling Taans and so the title **'Tanrus' (one who has a charming Taan) **was given to him by Bahadur Shah Zafar II, the last Mughal emperor.
 
• Occasionally Tanrus Khan sang **qawwalis** also.
 
• So he is also said to be a member of the** 'Qawwal Bachchon Ka Delhi Gharana'** originally organized by the legendary 13th-century musician **Amir Khusrow. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**__**Bade Ustad Ghulam Ali Khan**__

__
 
• **Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan** was an Indian** Hindustani classical vocalist**, from the **Patiala gharana.**
 
• Bade Ghulam amalgamated the best of three traditions into his own Patiala-Kasur style:
 
 
• **The Behram Khani elements of Dhrupad **
 
• **The gyrations of Jaipur **
 
• **The behlavas of Gwalior.**
 
 
 
• He received **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1962.**

**Ustad Amir Khan**__

__
 
• **Ustad Amir Khan** was one of the greatest and most influential** Indian vocalists in the Hindustani classical tradition.**
 
• He was the** founder of the Indore Gharana.**
 
• Although his singing style was an amalgamation of** Kirana** and **Bhendibazaar Gharanas**.
 
• He was a virtually **self-taught musician.**
 
• He developed his own gayaki influenced by the styles of** Abdul Waheed Khan, Rajab Ali Khan, and Aman Ali Khan**.

**Sadarang**__

 
• **Sadarang** was the** pen name of the Hindustani musical composer and artist Naimat Khan.**
 
• He was active in the eighteenth century.
 
• He and his nephew** Adarang** changed the Khayal style of Hindustani music into the form performed today.
 
• Naimat Khan composed Khyal for his disciples and he never performed Khyal.
 
• Sadarang served in the court of** Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah.**
 
• Sadarang and Adarang remain influential in Hindustani classical music, mainly through their compositions.

questions.question: Sher Khan defeated Humayun at Kanauj in the year ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun at the Battle of Kanauj in the year 1540.**
 
• The battle took place near the city of **Kanauj, located in present-day Uttar Pradesh, India**.
 
• Sher Shah Suri's forces, under his leadership, emerged victorious in this battle, resulting in Humayun's temporary expulsion from the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Humayun was able to regain his empire later and reclaim Delhi in 1555.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sher Shah Suri was born in 1486 in Sasaram, present-day Bihar, India.**

 
 
• He belonged to the Pashtun Sur tribe, hence the name **"Suri."**
 
• **Sher Shah Suri** initially served under the **Delhi Sultanate** and later joined the service of the **Mughal emperor Humayun.**
 
 
 
• **​Humayun, also known as Nasir-ud-Din Muhammad Humayun, was the second Mughal emperor who ruled over a significant portion of the Indian subcontinent.**
 
 
• He was born on **March 6, 1508,** in **Kabul, Afghanistan, and he ascended to the throne in 1530.**
 
• Humayun was the **eldest son of the first Mughal emperor, Babur.**
 
• During his reign, he faced several **challenges, including conflicts with regional rulers and internal power struggles.**
 
• Humayun's reign was marked by ups and downs, as he lost and regained his empire multiple times.

questions.question: Who among the following was given the charge of looking after the imperial household during the Mughal administration ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mir Saman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Khan-i-Saman,** alternatively known as Mir-i-Saman, held the esteemed position of overseeing the **Mughal Empire's imperial household**.
 
• This household, also referred to as the karkhanas, encompassed various factories and stores owned by the central government.
 
• As the head of the imperial household, Khan-i-Saman had multifaceted responsibilities, which included managing the karkhanas, overseeing stores, maintaining order, managing interactions, and handling internal relations.
 
• The Mughal imperial household accommodated the emperor, his wives, concubines, and relatives. Female servants and slaves were also part of the household staff, serving the needs of its members.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mir Bakshi **held the esteemed position of leading the Military Administration within the Mughal Empire. His duties encompassed gathering intelligence and providing recommendations regarding military appointments and promotions.
 
• In the Mughal Administration, the **Mir-i-Atish** served as the Head of the ordinance department, responsible for overseeing matters related to weaponry and artillery.
 
• **Mir-i-Bahar **was tasked with overseeing customs, as well as managing boats, ferry taxes, and port duties in coastal towns within the Mughal Empire.

questions.question: The first battle of Panipat took place between Babur and _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ibrahim Lodi.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **First battle of Panipat:-**

 
 
• **The first battle of Panipat took place between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi. **
 
• Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire, invaded India in 1526 and defeated the Sultan of Delhi, Ibrahim Lodi, in the first battle of Panipat.
 
• The battle was fought on April 21, 1526, near Panipat, which is now in the state of Haryana, India.
 
• The Mughal army was equipped with advanced weaponry, including artillery, which gave them an advantage over the Sultan's army.
 
• Ibrahim Lodi was killed in the battle, and Babur went on to establish the Mughal Empire in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Medini Rai: **

 
 
• Medini Rai (d. 1528) was a Rajput ruler of Chanderi state. The Battle of Chanderi was fought between Medini Rai and Babar in 1528. In this Babar was victorious and Medini Rai was killed.
 
 
 
• **Sikandar Lodi:**
 
 
• He was the second Sultan of the Lodi dynasty, who ruled from 1489 to 1517. He was not involved in the first battle of Panipat.
 
 
 
• **Rana Sanga:**
 
 
• He was a Rajput ruler of Mewar, who fought against Babur in the Battle of Khanwa in 1527.

questions.question: Which Mughal ruler was responsible for the execution of Guru Tegh Bahadur in the year 1675?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurangzeb**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the year 1675, Guru Tegh Bahadur was Killed in Delhi under the orders of the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb, the sixth Mughal emperor, of India.
 
• He was named head of the Sikh community after the death of the seven-year-old Guru Har Krishan.
 
• The name Guru Tegh Bahadur was given to him by Guru Hargobind.
 
• Sikh tradition says that the guru stood up for the interests of Kashmiri Pandits who approached him to intercede with the emperor on their behalf and to urge him to abolish a jizya (tax) recently levied.
 
• Convinced to stand up for the safety of the Kashmiri Pandits by his uncle, Gobind Rai, who later became Guru Gobind Singh, Guru Tegh Bahadur travelled to Delhi.
 
• In the late 17th century, Emperor Aurangzeb of Mughal levied Sharia law throughout his realm and an extra jizya levy on non-Muslims.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• At Bakala, Guru Tegh Bahadur meditated at the place for about 26 years 9 months 13 days.
 
• The ninth of the 10 Gurus of the Sikh religion was Guru Tegh Bahadur, revered as the ninth Nanak.
 
• The ninth of the 10 Gurus of the Sikh religion, Guru Tegh Bahadur died on November 24, in the year 1675.
 
• He is famously known for the protection he provided to the Sikhs and the Hindus against a 17th-century law that forced them to convert to Islam.
 
• His son Guru Gobind Singh, the last Guru of the Sikhs, transformed the community into a martial race to counter the might of the Mughals.
 
• ​Guru Tegh Bahadur was the ninth Sikh Guru, often venerated as the ‘Protector of Humanity’ (Srisht-di-Chadar) by the Sikhs.
 
 
• Known as a great teacher, Guru Tegh Bahadur was also an excellent warrior, thinker, and poet, who wrote detailed descriptions of the nature of God, mind, body, and physical attachments among other things spiritual.
 
• His writings are housed in the sacred text, ‘Guru Granth Sahib,’ in the form of 116 poetic hymns.
 
• He was also an avid traveller and played a key role in setting up preaching centres throughout the Indian subcontinent.
 
• During one such mission, he founded the town of Chak-Nanki in Punjab, which later became a part of Punjab’s Anandpur Sahib.
 
• In the year 1675, Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed in Delhi under the orders of the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb.

questions.question: Who among the following is credited with building Delhi’s Lāl Quilā (Red Fort)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shah Jahan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lāl Quilā​ **(Red Fort)

 
 
• The** Mughal Emperors' primary residence** was the **Red Fort, also known as Lal Qila, in Old Delhi, Delhi, India**.
 
• When **Shah Jahan chose to move his capital from Agra to Delhi on May 12, 1638, he ordered the Red Fort's construction**.
 
• Its original **colours were red and white**, and architect **Ustad Ahmad Lahori**, who also built the Taj Mahal, is credited with creating it. 
 
• The **fort**, built during Shah Jahan's era, is a prime example of **Mughal architecture and combines Persianate palace design with Indian customs**.
 
• **Nadir Shah's invasion of the Mughal Empire in 1739 **resulted in the **destruction of the fort's artwork and gems**. 
 
• The **fort's defensive walls** sustained little damage, and it was afterwards used as a garrison.
 
• The Indian flag was raised over the** Lahori Gate on August 15, 1947, by Jawaharlal Nehru, India's first prime minister**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Every year, the** Prime Minister hoisted the Indian tricolour flag** at the fort's main entrance and delivers a speech from its ramparts on **August 15, which marks India's Independence Day**.
 
• The Red Fort, which is a component of the Red Fort Complex, was designated a **UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007**.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about Akbar are true?

1 He introduced the Mansabdari system.

2 He defeated and merged the state of Bijapur in his empire.

3 He made Fatehpur Sikri his capital.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Only 1 and 3__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Akbar introduced the** Mansabdari system** to organize the military and administration.
 
• He established **Fatehpur Sikri** as his capital but later abandoned it due to water shortages.
 
• Akbar is known for his policy of religious tolerance and founded the **Din-i-Ilahi** to promote unity among different religions.
 
• He expanded the Mughal Empire significantly through both diplomacy and warfare, including the conquest of **Gujarat** and **Bengal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **‘Mansab**’ is an Arabic word meaning rank position or status of a person. 
 
• Mansabdari was a system in which the rank of a **government official **was determined. 
 
• Every** civil** and** military** officer was given a ‘mansab’. Different numbers which could be divided by ten were used for ranking officers.
 
• During the early reign of Akbar, the lowest grade was **ten **and the highest was **5000**. Towards the end of the reign, it was raised to **7000**.
 
• Higher Mansabs were given to **princes** and **Rajput** rulers who accepted the suzerainty of Akbar.
 
• the state of **Bijapur** was one of the most powerful states in South Asia, second to the Mughal Empire, which was conquered in **1686 **under **Aurangzeb**.

questions.question: Who amongst the following Mughal emperors got classical Hindu mythological texts Ramayana and Mahabharata translated into Persian?

The correct answer is__ Akbar__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Mahabharata was translated into Persian at Akbar’s orders, by Faizi and `Abd al-Qadir Bada’uni__ (c. 1540 – 1615) and named Razmnameh.
 
• Akbar
 __
 
• Akbar was the third Mughal emperor, who reigned from 1556 to 1605.
 
• Akbar succeeded his father, Humayun.
 
• Jahangir was his son.
 
• His abolition of Jajiya, his new religion Din-i-Ilahi, his land revenue policy, administrative policy etc. were such that his half century rule proved to be one of the brightest chapters in Indian History
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Jahangir

 
 
• Jahangir was a great patron of art and literature he spent lavishly in building splendid buildings and gardens and mausoleums.
 
• He was easily impressed by poets and writers especially those who wrote verses in his praise.
 
• Under his rule, he got constructed the Akbar's tomb, Idmaat ud Daulas tomb, and the famous Jahangir Fort.
 
 
 
• Aurangzeb
 
 
• Aurangzeb was the last important Mughal ruler and after him, the Mughal empire rapidly decayed and was finally put to an end by the British.
 
• This King reigned for half a century and died in 1707 leaving behind a war of succession.
 
 
 
• Humayun
 
 
• Humayun was the second emperor of the Mughal Empire, who ruled over territory in what is now Afghanistan, Pakistan, Northern India, and Bangladesh from 1530 to 1540 and again from 1555 to 1556.

questions.question: Which of the following books was translated as ‘The Razmnama’ (Book of War) during the reign of Akbar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahabharata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7814fad0832c466aebff87c249ff716b1a312e1faf18bc7d80fc5b49700b72d3.png] 

 
• 
 **Razmnama **is a** Persian translation of Mahabharata.**
 
 
• 
 Razmnama means **“book of war.**” It was completed by the maktab khana, **a translation bureau **set up by** Akbar **to translate important **Sanskrit texts into Persian.**
 
 
• 
 It was **Akbar’s intention** that the empire be** Persian-speaking, and translating the Hindu epics (including the Ramayana, the epic narrating the life of Ram)** was a way to encourage a **sense of belonging and inclusion amongst Hindu subjects**
 

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8cffad3867fadaf9184e5f66c0419468d3eaa4b7ce0a3bb824d755a4519f4607.png] 

**Akbar:**

 
• 
 ​**Akbar** was born as **Abu'l-Fath Jalal ud-din Muhammad Akbar on October 15, 1542.**
 
 
• 
 Akbar succeeded his father, **Humayun, in 1556** when he was **13 years old.**
 
 
• 
 Akbar was given the nickname **'the Great' **because of his** many accomplishments**.
 
 
• 
 Akbar had **nine ministers in his court,** who were called his **Navratnas or '9 gems'.**
 
 
• 
 He died in **1605.**

questions.question: The Battle of Khanua was fought between Babur and ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rana Sanga**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Battle of Khanua was fought between Babur and Rana Sanga**: 

 
 
• Babur: The founder of the Mughal Empire 
 
• Rana Sanga: The Rajput king of Mewar 
 
 
 
• The **battle took place on March 16, 152**7, near the village of Khanwa in the Bharatpur district of Rajasthan.
 
• The **battle was a major event in Medieval Indian history** and was one of the earliest battles in Northern India to use gunpowder extensively. 
 
• **Babur won** the battle and became the predominant ruler of central and northern India.
 
• He t**ook the title of Ghazi after his victory.**
 
• The** defeat of Rana Sanga at Khanwa is considered a watershed moment in the Mughal conquest of Northern India. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rana Ratan Singh**

 
 
• Rana Ratan Singh is perhaps most famously known for his **association with the legendary queen Padmini**.
 
• The story of her beauty and sacrifice has been immortalized in the epic poem "Padmini".
 
• **His reign was marked by the siege of Chittor by the Delhi Sulta**n, Alauddin Khilji, who was captivated by the tales of Padmini's beauty.
 
• The **siege led to a heroic sacrifice by the Rajput warriors**, including Jauhar, a form of self-immolation by women to protect their honour.
 
 
 
• **Maharana Pratap**
 
 
• Maharana Pratap is **one of the most celebrated figures in Indian history**, known for his unwavering courage and resistance against the Mughal Empire.
 
• His** most famous battle was the Battle of Haldighati**, where he fought against the formidable Mughal forces led by Akbar.
 
• Though the battle resulted in a tactical defeat, it showcased the indomitable spirit of the Rajput warriors.
 
• He is **revered as a symbol of Rajput pride** and a fighter for freedom.

questions.question: In the context of Mughal administration, which of the following is the most appropriate definition of 'Abwab'?

options.text: A tax levied on the lands over and above the original rent
A clerk in the government treasury

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** A tax levied on the lands over and above the original rent.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Abwab**__

 
 
• In Mughal India, **all temporary and circumstantial taxes and impositions levied by the government over and above regular taxes were called Abwabs.**
 
• All irregular impositions on** RAIYATS** above the established assessment of land in the PARGANA.
 
• Land tax was established by **Todar Mal **after a field-to-survey. 
 
• During the nawab period, a variety of abwabs were** imposed on ZAMINDARS,** who conveniently transferred them onto their raiyats.
 
• The practice of collecting abwabs began to decline from the 1920s.

questions.question: ________ administration became the model followed by the great emperor Akbar when he consolidated the Mughal Empire.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Sher Shah Suri__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Akbar followed the administration model of Sher Shah Suri.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Sher Shah Suri was the founder of the Suri Empire in India.

 
 
• He introduced the currency of the Rupee.
 
• Sher Shah of Sur took control of the Mughal Empire in 1540.
 
• His reorganization of the empire laid the foundations for the later Mughal emperors, notably Akbar, son of Humayun.
 
 
 
• Sher Shah Suri's administration:
 
 
• He organized an excellent administrative system.
 
• The king was aided by four important ministers.
 
 
• Diwan –i- Wizarat or Wazir – in charge of Revenue and Finance
 
• Diwan-i-Ariz – in charge of Army
 
• Diwan-i-Rasalat – Foreign Minister
 
• Diwan-i-Insha – Minister for Communications
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Akbar (1556- 1605)

 
 
• He reigned from 1556 to 1605.
 
• He defeated Hemu at the second battle of Panipat in 1556.
 
• He constructed Fatehpur Sikri and made it his capital in 1569.
 
• He started a new religion Din-i Ilahi in 1582.
 
• Abul Fazl wrote his biography titled Akbarnama.
 
• Nine of his courtiers were known as Navratnas.
 
 
• They were Todar Mal, Abul Fazal, Faizi, Birbal, Tansen, Abdur Rahim Khana-i-Khana, Mullah-do-Pyaza, Raja Man Singh, and Fakir Aziao-Din.
 
 
 
• He married a Hindu princess Harka Bai who is commonly known as Jodha Bai.
 
• Akbar captured the historic fortress of Chitor in 1568.
 
• He abolished the pilgrimage tax by Hindus in 1563.
 
• He abolished the Jizyah tax in 1564.
 
• He also introduced the Mansabdari System or the rank-holder system to organize the nobility and army.

questions.question: Tansen, one of the well-known musicians of medieval India, was in the court of which of the following Mughal emperors?

• **Born **in a **Hindu brahmin family**, he learned and **perfected his art **in the **northwest region **of **modern Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• **Tansen joined **the **musicians **at the **Mughal court of Akbar**.
 
• **Abu'l-Fath Jalal-ud-din Muhammad Akbar**, popularly known as **Akbar the Great**, and **also as Akbar**.
 
• He was the **third Mughal emperor**, who **reigned **from **1556 to 1605**.

__
 
• **Aurangzeb**__

 __
 
• **Aurangzeb **was the sixth emperor of the **Mughal Empire,** ruling from July 1658 until his death in 1707. 
 
• Under his emperorship, the Mughals reached their greatest extent with their territory spanning nearly the entirety of South Asia.
 
 
 
• **Babur**__
 __
 
• **Babur** was the founder of the Mughal Empire in the Indian subcontinent. 
 
• He was a** descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan** through his father and mother respectively.
 
 
 
• **Humayun **__
 
 
• **Humayun **was the second emperor of the Mughal Empire, who ruled over territory in what is now Eastern Afghanistan, Pakistan, Northern India, and Bangladesh from 1530 to 1540 and again from 1555 to 1556.

questions.question: Which amongst the following statements is correct about Mughal emperor Akbar ?

options.text: He fought and won the third battle of Panipat against the Hindu King Hemu.
He founded a new religion called ‘Din - e Ilahi’.
He was highly educated and knew many languages.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**He founded a new religion called 'Din - e llahi'**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Din - e Ilahi also known as the **"Religion of God"**.
 
• It was founded by The Mughal Emperor, Akbar(1556-1605) **in 1582**.
 
• It has the combined elements of **Islam, Hinduism, Jainism, Christianity and Zoroastrianism.**
 
• Akbar's full name was **"Jalal-ud-din Muhammad Akbar"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Akbar was the son of Emperor Humayun. Initially, his regent and guardian was **Bairam Khan**.
 
• The third battle of Panipat was fought between the **Maratha Empire** led by** Sadashivrao Bhau** and the** Durrani Empire** led by **Ahmad Shah Durrani**.
 
• The third battle of Panipat was** won by the Durrani Empire** and is known as one of the bloodiest wars of the 18th century.
 
• Akbar did not receive formal education, he could not read or write but could communicate in **Persian, Arabic, and Hindi.**
 
• Akbar established **Ibadat Khana(House of Worship)** for Scholars and Intellectuals in **Fatehpur Sikri**.
 
• Akbar court featured the** Navratnas(Nine Jewels),** a group of talented advisors.

questions.question: Humayun's Tomb situated in Delhi is built by_____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Biga Begum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Humayun's Tomb:

 
 
• The tomb of Humayun is located in Delhi.
 
• 
 
Humayun died in 1556, and his widow B**iga Begum​,** **also known as Haji Begam**, commenced the construction of his tomb in 1569, fourteen years after his death. It is the first distinct example of proper Mughal style, which was inspired by Persian architecture. It is well known that Humayun picked up the principles of Persian architecture during his exile, and he himself is likely to have planned the tomb, although there is no record to that effect. The tomb was constructed at a cost of 15 lakh rupees (1.5 million).

 
 
• 
 
Mirak Mirza Ghiyath, a Persian, was the architect employed by Haji Begam for this tomb.

 
 
• It was also the first structure of its size to use red sandstone.
 
• In 1993, the tomb was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

• Humayun was the eldest son of Babar.
 
• In the Battle of Chausa, in 1539 and Battle of Bilgram, in 1540 (Battle of Kanauj), Humayun was defeated by Sher Khan.
 
• After losing his kingdom, Humayun became an exile for the next 15 years.

• He loved painting and wrote poetry in the Persian language.

questions.question: Who among the following wrote a history of Akbar’s reign titled Akbar Nama?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Abul Fazl**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The Akbarnama, which translates to Book of Akbar (1556-1605), the 3rd Mughal Emperor, was written by his court historian and biographer, Abul Fazl.
 
• It was written in Persian originally, which was the court language of the Mughals.
 
• The book includes vivid and detailed descriptions of his life and times during the reign of Akbar.
 
• It is believed it took seven years for the book to be completed.
 
• Abul Fazl was one of the Nine Jewels of the Akbar Court.
 
• The first volume of the book deals with the birth of Akbar, the history of Timur's family and the reigns of Babur and Humayun, and the Suri sultans of Delhi. 
 
• The second volume describes the detailed history of the reign of Akbar till the year 1602 and records the events during Akbar's reign.
 
• It also throws light on how Bairam Khan and Akbar won the second Battle of Panipat (1556) against Hemu.
 
• The third volume of the Akbarnama describes the administrative system of the Empire. It also deals with Akbar's household, army, revenues, and geography of the Mughal Empire.
 
• It also provides us the information about the traditions and culture of the people living in India at that time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**__ ____About Abul Fazl :__​

__
 
• Abul Fazl was the grand courtier of the Mughal emperor Akbar.
 
• He was the author of the Akbarnama, the official history of Akbar's reign.
 
• Apart from Akbarnama, Abul Fazl also wrote the Persian translation of the Bible.
 
• He was also one of the Nine Jewels of the Akbar's royal court and the brother of Faizi, the poet laureate of Akbar.

Nine Jewels of Akbar:__ 

 
• The following were the Nine Jewels or Navratnas of the Akbar's Royal Court-
 
• Raja Birbal- He was a noble who won Akbar’s appreciation for his wits.
 
• Tansen-He was the musician in Akbar’s court.
 
• Abul Fazal- He was the chief advisor in the court of Akbar.
 
• Faizi- Faizi was a poet who was famous for his work Nal U Daman.
 
• Raja Man Singh- He was the General in the court of Akbar.
 
• Raja Todar Mal- He was the Finance minister in the court of Akbar.
 
• Mullah Do Piazza- Home Minister of Akbar.
 
• Fakir Aziao-Din- Religious Minister of Akbar.
 
• Abdul Rahim Khan-I-Khana- Defence Minister of Akbar and a renowned poet.
